comments: NPU-legality fix for the stem_stride=1 result. The eltwise-add on this hardware has no usable activation stage -- an add must be followed by a conv, which supplies the nonlinearity via its own act_type -- so the previous run's three bottleneck blocks (act_elt(pw_linear(dw(x)) + x), i.e. add -> leaky with nothing between) are not deployable, even though they trained to val dice 0.6401 / test 0.6556. See CLAUDE.md's 'Eltwise-add activation' section; export_int8.py now refuses to export the illegal form. This config sets eltwise_act='linear': the block becomes y = pw_linear(dw(x)) + x and the following conv applies leaky, which is pre-activation ResNet ordering. Zero extra MACs, zero extra parameters, and the state_dict is unchanged -- so this is initialized by finetuning directly from the illegal run's own val_doppler_model.pt (strict=True load, verified) rather than from the native checkpoint or from scratch. Everything else is identical to kuralsnet_npu_seg_8x64_stemstride1_finetune_leaky0125_wq2x1.json (stem_stride=1, encoder_depth=1, bottleneck_ch=64, kernel3, dropout 0.1, leaky slope 0.125, w_eff=2w+1, quant_freeze_iters=76000), so the only changed variable is where the bottleneck's nonlinearity sits. Target: match or beat 0.6401 while being exportable.
